sections.heading: Is It a Good Idea to Spray Foam Your Roof?

runs.v: Can spray foam be applied to a roof? Yes: over a structurally sound, dry flat or low-slope roof, spray foam is a good idea, because it insulates, waterproofs, and adds little weight in one retrofit. It is a poor fit over a wet or multi-layer roof, on a steep roof, or where the building cannot schedule the dry, mild weather the foam needs. How long does a spray foam roof last? 30 or more years with the coating maintained, and longer with recoats. It is crucial to hire a registered, insured contractor with specialized experience in SPF systems, and GAF Certified contractors offer enhanced warranties on GAF systems.

sections.heading: Spray Foam Roofing vs. Attic Insulation and Basement Insulation

runs.v: Spray foam insulation contractors across the New York and New Jersey area mostly spray foam insulation inside buildings: attic insulation, basement insulation, and wall cavities. Interior spray foam insulation creates an airtight barrier that seals gaps and drafts, can be applied in hard-to-reach areas, and can last throughout the life of your home, over 50 years with proper care; closed-cell foam gives higher thermal resistance per inch than fiberglass or cellulose. Interior foam generally must sit behind a thermal barrier such as ½-inch gypsum board, per the International Residential Code. A spray foam roof is a different system: the foam goes on top of the roof deck as the roof itself, under a UV coating, and this page covers that roof system.

Why are people removing spray foam insulation? Mostly for interior foam: poorly mixed foam can leave lingering odors, and foam sprayed under a roof deck can hide roof leaks and deck moisture from an inspection. A spray foam roof sits on top of the deck, where leaks can be found and repaired, which lets owners inspect the roof like any other.

N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires full removal of a water-soaked roof or one with 2 or more layers, and a recover avoids tear-off disruption on an occupied apartment building or storefront.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for spray foam roofing in East Orange?

runs.v: On a commercial, multi-family, or attached East Orange building, recovering or replacing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Reroofing a detached one- or two-family house is ordinary maintenance with no construction permit; applications go to the Department of Property Maintenance at East Orange City Hall.
